title: Ray Gun Bryan Ferry interview in Zapf Dingbats
titleBreak: Ray Gun Bryan Ferry interview|in Zapf Dingbats
lede: The 1994 Ray Gun spread in which David Carson set a whole Bryan Ferry interview in the symbol font Zapf Dingbats.
summary: Justified columns made entirely of dingbat symbols, with giant dingbats over the headline. David Carson, Ray Gun, 1994.

source.label: Sharan Shetty, “The Rise And Fall Of Grunge Typography”, The Awl (2012), archived copy

made: 1994 (The Awl); issue number not stated by the sources

evidence.note: Inspected a 1100 × 697 photograph of the opened spread, posted on the Process & Skills student blog (2013), in a scratchpad copy; The Awl’s own copy is 640 px wide. The owner of the photographed copy and the issue number are not stated. Not stored.

styles.note: Clear example of the style’s attitude: legibility is abandoned on purpose. Partial fit for its surface, because the dingbats are clean and the ground is not dirty.

context: The Awl says Carson disliked a Ray Gun article on Bryan Ferry and set the entire spread in Zapf Dingbats, in a 1994 issue. [The Awl](https://web.archive.org/web/20150925150838/http://www.theawl.com/2012/08/grunge-typography).
Wikipedia cites the Ferry interview as the example of Ray Gun’s not always readable “grunge typography”. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Gun_(magazine)).
observed: The right-hand page and most of the left are justified columns made entirely of Zapf Dingbats symbols: stars, circles, triangles, crosses, and arrows.
A grey rectangle sits behind part of the dingbat text and crosses the gutter.
The headline “bryan ferry” is a lowercase serif, partly covered by a large maroon four-lobed dingbat and a yellow-green photograph of Ferry in an armchair.
A large olive asterisk-like dingbat and a row of grey stars and flowers act as display ornaments.
The photo credit under the picture is the only readable text.
interpretation: The spread is grunge as a gesture rather than as a texture: it uses a clean, standard font to make text unreadable. It belongs in the collection for its intent and for how often it is cited, not for its surfaces.
borrow: Use a symbol font as a grey texture that has the rhythm of text, in a decorative area only.
Enlarge single dingbats to poster size and let them cover a headline.

rights.statement: No image is stored. David Carson is living, so the design is in copyright. Photographs by their sources.
